title.narrative: Output 3.4. Increased capacity of ILO constituents to promote peaceful, stable and resilient societies through decent work

description.narrative: In partnership with the Ministry of Labour and the Ministry of Social Affairs, more than 30 municipalities fulfilled parts of their action plan through the ILO implementation of community infrastructure projects under the EIIP. The Ministry of Transport and Public Works also achieved maintenance of several vital roads through the same programme. Under the ILO EIIP Lebanon programme, funded by Germany through KFW, and having the Ministry of Labour and the Ministry of Social Affairs as main governmental partners, the ILO has implemented since January 2020 more than 16 projects. These interventions are at the heart of the humanitarian-development-peace nexus and have generated since January 2020 more than 280,000 worker-days to more than 5400 beneficiaries. By the end of 2021,The ILO will have provided training opportunities for 5 MoL and MoSA staff on "Ending violence and harassment in the world of work" and "Designing public employment programs for sustainable recovery" enhancing the capacity of the Public Sector to facilitate the implementation of employment intensive programs. ILO is working on improved participation of women in employment generation interventions where it has reached around 25% for the above mentioned projects. The ILO has trained more than 80 private sector contractors, as well as development partners and livelihood actors like UN agencies and local and international NGOs to implement employment intensive programmes and Local resource based technology ( LRBT) approaches for sustainable infrastructure development, maintenance and environmental works.

Output 3.3. Increased capacity of member States to formulate and implement policies for a just transition towards environmentally sustainable economies and societies

description.narrative: The Ministry of Labour (MoL) and the Ministry of Social Affairs (MoSA) endorsed the guidelines for EIP (Employment intensive projects) in November 2020, which includes environmentally sound principles as an integral part of the design and implementation of EIP activities with a balanced protection and use of natural resources. Under the ILO Employment Intensive Investment Programme (EIIP), funded by Germany through KFW, the ILO supported the government (MoSA and MoL) and led the development of the guidelines, taking a participatory approach through consultation with government and actors in the livelihood sector. The ILO incorporated measures to comply with relevant environmental safeguards standards into the design of all EIP infrastructure works. The EIIP Lebanon monitored compliance with Lebanon's environmental protection law to ensure that any required mitigation measures are put in place for EIP projects.

Output 3.2. Increased capacity of member States to formulate and implement policies and strategies for creating decent work in the rural economy

description.narrative:
Within the implementation of the agricultural input voucher programme, which is one of the leading programmes under the Lebanon National Agriculture Strategy (2020–2025), led by the Ministry of Agriculture, 500 Lebanese vulnerable farmers from Akkar, North Lebanon, Bekaa and Baalbeck-Hermel accessed agricultural inputs that are key to maintain production. Farmers received support in improving farm management and OSH of farm workers. This initiative will contribute to safeguarding jobs of farmers and their workers in the context of the COVID-19 pandemic and the financial crisis in Lebanon.
Within the national efforts to improve capacity to provide career guidance and job matching services as well as boosting access to formal jobs in rural areas, a pilot was implemented in one of the Community Development Centres (CDC) in the rural governorate of Akkar by integrating career guidance and employment services, such as career counselling, soft skills, labour rights and obligations awareness sessions, support in obtaining work permits, on the job training placements, and referrals to skills training and short-term employment opportunities, in the CDC support services to Lebanese and Syrian refugees in rural Akkar. Based on the assessment "Unlocking opportunities for decent job creation in Lebanon's horticulture sector" in April 2020, the horticulture market system for decent job creation strategy was developed to harness the potential of the sector for refugee-inclusive growth, and includes interventions to increase economic opportunities and benefits for Lebanese farming households whilst also improving job prospects, working conditions and incomes for refugees in Lebanon's horticulture sector, as well as improving export opportunities for small and medium-sized rural enterprises. To advance the policy discussions on decent work in agriculture, a policy paper on refugees' access to formal and decent employment in agriculture was developed. Under the ILO PROSPECTS programme, funded by the Netherlands, and in collaboration with FAO, ILO contributed to technical support to selected small-scale farmers in Lebanon. ILO also provided capacity development for farmers in terms of management skills and OSH of farm workers. Also, under the ILO PROSPECTS, and building synergies with the Danish Refugee Council (DRC) and UNHCR, the ILO collaborated in the pilot in one of the Community Development Centers in rural Akkar with the integration of career guidance and employment services activities. As a result of this pilot intervention, 181 Syrian refugees and vulnerable Lebanese sreceived tailored career counselling with a 99% satisfaction rate, participated in soft skills trainings and enhanced their skills and capacities to access the labour market, and received awareness sessions on decent work conditions; 30 individuals were placed in WorkBased Learning (WBL) opportunities; and 47 individuals got referred to employment opportunities and placed in jobs. The results showed the participation of almost 60% Syrians and 40% Lebanese with an approximate female to male ration of 3:1. Also, under PROSPECTS, the ILO provided technical support in the development of a market assessment of the Lebanese horticulture sector, and provided subsequent technical assistance to carry out a market systems analysis to formulate a strategy for decent job creation in the sector.
